categories.name: Defense articles — military / munitions
categories.summary: Items specially designed for a military application are generally controlled under the ITAR, not the EAR. Export almost always requires State Department (DDTC) authorization regardless of destination.

categories.name: Information Security — encryption / cybersecurity
categories.summary: Products that perform or use 'non-standard' cryptography for confidentiality can be controlled under 5A002/5D002. Most mass-market commercial encryption qualifies for License Exception ENC after a self-classification or CCATS, but it is still classified, not EAR99.

categories.name: Electronics — semiconductors, ICs & fabrication
categories.summary: Advanced integrated circuits, RF/microwave components, FPGAs, ADCs/DACs above performance thresholds, and the equipment, materials and software to design or fabricate them are controlled in Category 3. Recent rules add tight controls on advanced-node logic, HBM and AI accelerators.

categories.name: Computers — high-performance computing
categories.summary: Digital computers and 'electronic assemblies' above an Adjusted Peak Performance threshold, plus interconnect and certain intrusion/cyber tools, are controlled in Category 4. Most laptops/servers are EAR99 but clusters, accelerator nodes and HPC interconnect may not be.

categories.name: Sensors & Lasers — imaging, optics, lasers
categories.summary: Focal plane arrays, thermal/infrared cameras, image intensifiers, high-speed cameras, certain lasers, magnetometers, gravimeters and radar are controlled in Category 6. Thresholds turn on wavelength, frame rate, sensitivity and power.

categories.name: Navigation & Avionics — inertial, GNSS, flight control
categories.summary: Accelerometers, gyroscopes, inertial measurement/navigation units, certain GNSS receivers (high-altitude/high-velocity), and flight control systems are controlled in Category 7, frequently for Missile Technology reasons.

categories.name: Aerospace & Propulsion — aircraft, UAV, engines, space
categories.summary: Gas turbine engines, UAVs/drones, rockets, launch vehicles, spacecraft, satellites and their components and production technology are controlled in Category 9, heavily for Missile Technology and Spacecraft reasons.

categories.name: Marine — submersibles, underwater systems
categories.summary: Submersibles, underwater vehicles, marine propulsion, syntactic foam, closed-circuit diving systems and underwater sensors are controlled in Category 8.

categories.name: Materials Processing — machine tools, robots, bearings
categories.summary: Multi-axis CNC machine tools, precision bearings, isostatic presses, spin/flow-forming machines, robots for hazardous environments and dimensional inspection systems are controlled in Category 2, often for nuclear/missile reasons.

categories.name: Advanced Materials & Chemicals
categories.summary: High-strength fibers and composites, specialty alloys, energetic materials, precursor chemicals, biological agents and protective equipment are controlled in Category 1, including for chemical/biological and missile reasons.

categories.name: Nuclear — materials, reactors & enrichment
categories.summary: Nuclear materials, reactors, centrifuges, heavy water, tritium and related production equipment are tightly controlled. Some items fall under NRC (Part 110) or DOE (Part 810) jurisdiction rather than the EAR.

categories.name: Telecommunications — RF & networking
categories.summary: Certain radios, jamming/anti-jam equipment, phased arrays, mobile communication interception and high-speed/undersea transmission gear are controlled in Category 5 Part 1. Ordinary commercial networking is usually EAR99.

highRiskDestinations.note: Comprehensively sanctioned / embargoed destination — nearly all exports require a license and most are prohibited. Treat any shipment as license-required pending OFAC/BIS review.
Subject to broad Russia/Belarus industry-sector controls and an expanded license requirement / denial policy. Most items beyond basic consumer goods require a license.
Subject to expanded controls for advanced computing, semiconductors and military end-use/end-user (MEU) rules. Screen end-use and end-user carefully.
Subject to a US arms embargo or partial sanctions — defense and many dual-use items face a license requirement and a policy of denial.
